title: Finite equivariant quotient presentations of profinite actions
statement: Use the small representatives of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff topological group with an open-normal-subgroup neighbourhood basis at the identity, and let $P$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space with a continuous left action $G\times P\to P$. A finite clopen partition is a finite collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets with union $P$; the empty partition of the empty space is allowed. A partition is $G$-invariant if $G$ permutes its parts. Every finite clopen partition admits a finer finite $G$-invariant clopen partition. The $G$-invariant finite clopen partitions, ordered by refinement, form a small cofiltered inverse system of finite discrete continuous $G$-sets $P_i$ (the parts), with surjective quotient maps. The canonical map $P\to\varprojlim_i P_i$, sending a point to its part in each partition, is a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism. Here the limit is the space of compatible families, with subspace topology from the product of the finite discrete sets and coordinatewise action. Conversely, for any small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$ and inverse system of finite discrete continuous $G$-sets $Q_i$, its compatible-family limit $Q\subseteq\prod_i Q_i$ is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space with continuous coordinatewise $G$-action. Empty stages and the empty limit are allowed in this assertion.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28: pro-objects in finite discrete G-sets are profinite continuous G-sets. The invariant-partition detail is the compact-action refinement argument; compare Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY (lemma-profinite) for the underlying clopen-partition construction.
